requirements.findings: The warning-suppression path filters by prefix, not by containment. `hide_qt_warning(pattern)` installs `QtWarningFilter`, and `QtWarningFilter.filter()` suppresses a record only when `record.msg.strip().startswith(self._pattern)` is false-negated, i.e. prefix matches are filtered and non-prefix matches are logged. The current unit tests verify this exact behavior: with pattern `World`, `Hello World` is logged unchanged; with pattern `Hello`, `Hello`, `Hello World`, and `  Hello World  ` are all suppressed. This means occurrences of the pattern later in the warning text are not treated as matches for suppression, so the current implementation does not satisfy a requirement for whole-message containment matching.
